target.title: fix(outbound): restore current-conversation binding map when persist fails
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where plugin channels that use the generic current-conversation binding (any channel without a custom binding adapter) could route inbound messages to the wrong or a deleted session target after a failed durable write. The binding mutators — bind, touch, unbind, and expiry prune-on-read — update the process-wide in-memory binding map first and then persist it to SQLite. If the persist throws (disk full, read-only DB, transaction failure), the map is left ahead of disk. Because the map is only loaded from disk once per process (`bindingsLoaded` is a one-time flag), the diverged bindings are then served for the rest of the process lifetime — until a restart — even though the caller already received the error. Inbound messages get delivered to a stale binding (a resolved session that was actually unbound, or a target that never persisted). The one-time load path has the same weakness in the other direction: it flips `bindingsLoaded` and clears the map before the DB read completes, so a failing initial read latches an empty cache until restart. ## Why This Change Was Made Each mutating path now snapshots the in-memory map, and if the durable write throws it restores that snapshot before rethrowing, so runtime state never drifts ahead of disk. This mirrors the rollback pattern already merged for the cron scheduler in #99960 (`persistOrRestore` in `src/cron/service/ops.ts`). The unbind-by-session path snapshots after its expiry scan settles (that scan can itself persist prune deletes), so a later batch failure cannot resurrect a binding the scan already dropped from disk. The one-time load now reads into a local first and marks the cache loaded only after the read succeeds. Scope is deliberately narrow: no change to the write mechanism, the store schema, or the broader session-binding surface. The snapshot is a shallow map copy, which is sufficient because records are always replaced wholesale (never mutated in place), keeping the hot binding paths cheap. ## User Impact Operators no longer end up with a process serving conversation bindings that disagree with what is on disk after a transient storage failure. A failed mutation now leaves the in-memory state exactly as it was before the attempt, and the error still surfaces to the caller. No config, API, or behavior change on the success path. Affected paths: bind, touch, unbind by binding id, unbind by target session key, and the expiry prune-on-read. ## Evidence ### Real-behavior proof — genuine shared-SQLite write failure Drives the real production path (`bindGenericCurrentConversation` → `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`) against a real `state/openclaw.sqlite`, and injects a **genuine durable-write failure** (not a mock): `PRAGMA query_only = ON` on the production cached state connection, so the next write transaction raises `SQLITE_READONLY`. It then compares disk ground-truth (read straight from the `current_conversation_bindings` table) against what a caller is served by `resolveGenericCurrentConversationBinding`. Same recipe merged for #99960. `bind` conversation → `session-A` (persists), inject the fault, then re-`bind` the same conversation → `session-B` (write throws): **BEFORE (main `5e22787ba1`, no rollback):** ``` [fault] bind B threw : Error: attempt to write a readonly database [after] disk ground-truth : [ 'agent:codex:acp:session-A' ] [after] resolve() serves : agent:codex:acp:session-B RESULT: DIVERGENCE — caller served agent:codex:acp:session-B but disk holds agent:codex:acp:session-A (BUG present) ``` The caller saw the write error, disk still holds `session-A`, yet the in-memory map serves `session-B` — a target that never persisted. Because `bindingsLoaded` is a one-time flag, this phantom binding is served until process restart. **AFTER (this PR `bcd4668cb2`, with rollback):** ``` [fault] bind B threw : Error: attempt to write a readonly database [after] disk ground-truth : [ 'agent:codex:acp:session-A' ] [after] resolve() serves : agent:codex:acp:session-A RESULT: CONSISTENT — caller served agent:codex:acp:session-A, matches disk (rollback worked) ``` Same genuine `SQLITE_READONLY`, same surfaced error, but the map is rolled back to the last-persisted state — the caller is served what is actually on disk.
Harness (node --import tsx proof.mts, temp OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR) ```ts const CONV = { channel: "workspace", accountId: "default", conversationId: "C-real-proof" }; const SESSION_A = "agent:codex:acp:session-A"; const SESSION_B = "agent:codex:acp:session-B"; function setQueryOnly(on: boolean): void { // Toggle the production cached connection read-only so the next real write // transaction raises a genuine SQLITE_READONLY (like a read-only mount). openOpenClawStateDatabase().db.exec(`PRAGMA query_only = ${on ? "ON" : "OFF"};`); } // 1. Durably persist conversation -> SESSION_A via the real production path. await bindGenericCurrentConversation({ targetSessionKey: SESSION_A, targetKind: "session", conversation: CONV }); // 2. Inject a genuine durable-write failure on the shared SQLite connection. setQueryOnly(true); // 3. Re-bind same conversation -> SESSION_B; the real write transaction throws. try { await bindGenericCurrentConversation({ targetSessionKey: SESSION_B, targetKind: "session", conversation: CONV }); } catch (err) { /* caller sees the write error */ } // 4. Lift the fault, read disk ground-truth, observe what resolve() serves. setQueryOnly(false); const disk = /* SELECT target_session_key FROM current_conversation_bindings */; const inMemory = resolveGenericCurrentConversationBinding(CONV)?.targetSessionKey; // BEFORE: inMemory === SESSION_B (diverges from disk SESSION_A). AFTER: inMemory === SESSION_A. ```
### Focused fault-injection tests `src/infra/outbound/current-conversation-bindings.test.ts` covers each mutating path (bind, touch, unbind-by-id, unbind-by-session, prune-on-read), the mixed unbind-by-session case where an expired binding is pruned mid-scan before the batch fails, and a failing initial load that must not latch an empty cache. Same proof shape merged for the cron rollback in #99960. ``` $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/current-conversation-bindings.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 17 passed (17) # 10 existing + 7 new ``` - `pnpm tsgo:core` — clean (0 type errors) - oxlint / oxfmt — clean
